runs.text: The concept of the Second Coming of Jesus Christ to Earth is a central doctrine in Christianity. This event is prophesied in various Biblical texts, including the book of Revelation and the Gospels. When Christ returns, believers are expected to receive new bodies, which are often described as glorified and imperishable (See 1 Corinthians 15:42-44). These new bodies are not subject to decay, pain, or death, symbolizing eternal life with God.
IMMORTALITY:
1. When will the redeemed put on incorruptibility and immortality?
1 Corinthians 15:52
In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump
: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible,
and we shall be changed.
For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality
Note:
At the Second Coming the redeemed will finally become incorruptible and immortal.
2. What do Christians wait eagerly for while they are living in this world?
Romans 8:22
For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now. 23 And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit,
even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body
3. What happens to our bodies when He comes again?
Philippians 3:20
For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ: 21
Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body
, according to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things unto himself.
Note:

At the Second Coming of Jesus, our bodies will be transformed and freed from sin's corruption. Until then, our righteousness is solely in Christ. Our flesh remains corrupted. Only our character, heart, and mind can be renewed before His return.
HOLD ON TO YOUR FAITH:
4. For us to experience this ultimate salvation, what must we do?
2 Timothy 4:7
I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness,
which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and
not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.
Note:

The Bible gives full assurance of salvation to believers. But the Bible does not say that “once saved, always saved.” As long as we have faith in Christ, our salvation is guaranteed, but the moment we turn our back on Christ through unbelief, we are also turning our back on the faith required for salvation in Christ.
5. What warning does the Bible give to those who are tempted to give up their faith in Christ?
Hebrews 10:37
For yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry. 38
Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him.
But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul
6. What advice did Jesus give to His disciples?
Matthew 10:22
And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake:
but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
Note:

Christians live in a sinful world that rejects Christ and is influenced by Satan. Because of this, we face many trials. However, this suffering is only temporary. Instead of dwelling on present hardships, we should focus on Christ, who will deliver us at His second coming.
7. Why are we to hold fast to what we have?
Revelation 3:11
Behold, I come quickly:
hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown
8. Was the prodigal son able to repent and return to his father?
Luke 15:21
And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.
But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:
And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:
For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
Note:

This is a story that Jesus told of a son who took his inheritance and squandered it with his partying friends. When the money was all gone, he returned to his father and his father received him with gladness.
When we repent, our Father will receive us also. Our salvation is not based on “once saved, always saved.” Our salvation is based on believing on the Son of God!
MILLENNIUM:
9. What will be said just before the second advent?
1 Thessalonians 5:2
For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. 3
For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them,
as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape. 4 But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief.
Note:

Today, there is much talk about “1,000 years of peace and safety”, “A Golden Age”, but Christians must not be deceived by such talk. The Bible is clear that at such a time, sudden destruction will take place.
10. What precedes the millennium?
Revelation 20:4

I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.
Note:

The millennium does not usher in 1,000 years of peace. Instead, it follows the tribulation and the beheading of those who follow Jesus. This will happen to many who do not receive the mark of the beast.
11. Resurrection / 2nd coming precedes a millennium.
Revelation 20:6
. Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the
first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power,
but they shall be priests of God and of Christ,
and shall reign with him a thousand years.
Note:
The millennium is after the resurrection!
Therefore, it also has to be after the second coming!
What this means is that there will be a false promise of a golden age before Jesus returns. This is a snare for those who look for peace and safety where there is no peace.
12. What will be tested during the great tribulation?
Luke 18:8
Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?
Note:

During the great tribulation, the supreme test will be the faith of the believers. Before Jesus returns, God will produce a people whose faith in Christ will be unshakable, even though they feel forsaken by God. This seems to be the opposite of a golden age!
13. Before Christ comes, what will the last generation of Christians experience?
Jeremiah 30:7
Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it:
it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble
; but he shall be saved out of it.
Note:

The time of Jacob’s trouble is during the great tribulation. When Jacob wrestled with the angel, his faith did not let go until he received the desired blessing. Those looking for peace and safety will neglect to develop this faith.
JESUS IS COMING SOON:
14. What admonition does Jesus give to believers?
Luke 12:40
Be ye therefore ready also: for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.
Note:
The Bible warns us that the second coming of Christ will take even the Christians by surprise. That is why we must always be ready by keeping our faith focused on Christ.
15. What will happen if you are not waiting and watching for the second advent?
1 Thessalonians 5:3
For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them,
as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape. 4
But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief.
Note:

To come as a thief in the night means that the coming of Christ will be at an unexpected time, even for Christians. Therefore, we must not be fooled by those who cry for peace and safety. When they cry for peace and safety they are actually saying that Christ’s second coming cannot be near. This is a deception! (See Revelation 16:15)
FALSE SIGNS AND WONDERS:
16. What other deception are we to be aware of?
Matthew 24:24
For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.
Note:
This is one of the strongest warnings in all of the Bible. There will be false manifestations of Christ before the true second coming. There are also false prophets.
17. What does the devil transform himself into?
2 Corinthians 11:14
And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light
Note:
The only way to tell the false Christ from the true Son of God is through Scripture alone!
18. If we hear that Christ is in the desert or in the secret chambers, what are we to do?
Matthew 24:26
Wherefore if they shall say unto you, Behold, he is in the desert; go not forth: behold, he is in the secret chambers; believe it not.
MEET THE LORD IN THE AIR:
19. How shall the Son of man come?
Matthew 24:27
For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be
Note:

Scripture alone will keep us safe from the overwhelming deceptions of the end days. False Christs will appear. And even Satan himself will appear as Christ. But God’s people will not be deceived. God’s people know that Christ’s coming will look like lightning shining from the east even to the west. The redeemed will exclaim on that day: “Lo, this
is
our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us.” (See Isaiah 25:9)
20. Where will the saints meet the Lord?
1 Thessalonians 4:16
For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air
: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.
Note:

The dead will be raised, then we which are alive will be caught up to meet the Lord in the clouds. God’s people who read the Bible know that when Christ returns the second time, He will never touch this earth, because the saints will meet Him in the air. This means that all beings walking upon this earth who claim to be Jesus are false. Satan can only fool those who do not know what the scriptures say about the second coming of Christ.
A CLEVER COUNTERFEIT:
Prior to 1830, no church taught the pre-tribulation rapture in their creed, or statement of belief.

Strange as it may seem, the rapture doctrine is not Biblical; it was invented by John Nelson Darby! The entire secret rapture theory is built upon a constant repetition of words and ideas that are not found in the Bible. But they have been repeated so often that millions have assumed that they must be Biblical. We will take a look at some of the texts that have been used to support this non-Biblical doctrine of a two-phase 2nd coming .

Oswald Smith, a noted minister and author from Toronto, Canada, says in his booklet, “Tribulation or Rapture,” that he once held the two-stage teaching. But, when he began to search the Scriptures for himself, he discovered that there is not a single verse in the Bible to uphold this heretical view. He confessed: "I had been taught that the Greek word '
parousia

' (coming) always referred to the rapture and that other words were used for the coming of Christ in glory ... but I found that this is not true. We might go through all the writers of the New Testament, and we would fail to discover any indication of the so-called 'two stages' of our Lord's coming. This theory was invented by man.
Search and see, there are no verses in the Bible that even mention it

The Bible clearly teaches that Jesus Christ will come the second time in glory and majesty to take His redeemed home with Him. It will be a personal, visible, and earth-shaking event that every living person will know about. The righteous will be caught up to meet the Lord in the air (1 Thessalonians 4:17), whereas the wicked will be slain by the brightness of Christ’s coming.
21. How long did Jesus promise to be with the church?
Matthew 28:20
lo, I am with you alway,
even unto the end of the world.
Amen.
Note:
Why would Jesus promise to be with the church until the end of the world if He intended to come 7-years before the end of the world? That promise would then have no meaning!
22. How will Jesus destroy the earth when He comes as a thief in the night?
2 Peter 3:10
But the day of the Lord will come
as a thief in the night
in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise,
and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up
Note:

If coming as a thief is the secret rapture that takes place seven years before the end of the world, how can the elements melt, and the heavens and earth “pass away” seven years before the world ends? Does this make sense?
23. What promise does Jesus give to those who kept the word of His patience?
Revelation 3:10
Because thou hast
kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth
Note:

This text does not speak of the righteous leaving this world. This text is telling us that those who keep the word of His patience will be able to stand through their hour of temptation. The devil will “try them”, but they will be able to stand!
24. Does Daniel 9:24-27 teach a 7-year tribulation period?
Daniel 9:24-27

Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy

Know therefore and understand, that from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks: the street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times

And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.

And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate.
A day in Bible prophecy symbolizes a “year”. (See Numbers 14:34; Ezekiel 4:6)
** There is no year 0 A.D.; thus one year must be added in calculating the timeline.
Note:

Since so much of the rapture theology revolves around the seven-year period, one would assume that the Bible must speak frequently of such a time period. But not so. There is not one single scriptural reference that ties the seven years to the end of the world or the coming of Christ. Most rapture literature mentions the seven-year tribulation period without ever offering any Bible proof or explanation. Millions have assumed that it must be so well documented that no proof is needed, but in fact, the opposite is true. There just isn't any evidence to give.

Most Bible students are amazed to learn that those who believe in the rapture try to justify their seven years by lifting a prophecy of Daniel completely out of its context. In Daniel 9:24-27 God made a daring prophecy concerning the probation of the nation of Israel. He said to Daniel, "Seventy weeks *['weeks of years' RSV] are determined upon thy people to finish transgression, and to make an end of sins" (v. 24). Please notice that God was going to allow Daniel's people (the Jews) seventy weeks to get ready for the Messiah. The seventy weeks are prophetic time, meaning that each day represents a literal year (See Ezekiel 4:6). So the seventy weeks would be a literal period of 490 years, after which the Israelites would no longer be God's people. They would be rejected as a nation because of their rejection of the Messiah.

In Daniel 9:25, the prophecy of the seventy weeks was to begin with the decree to restore and build Jerusalem. This well-known date is 457 B.C., when Artaxerxes sent out the decree (See Ezra 7:13). From that date (457 B.C.) the Jews would have exactly 490 years to finish filling up their cup of iniquity by rejecting the Messiah. That 490-year probation ended in **A.D. 34, when the Jews ceased to be God's chosen people. Daniel 9:25 says that the Messiah would be anointed after sixty-nine of those prophetic weeks had passed by. That would be 483 years from the decree date of 457 B.C. It brings us to the year A.D. 27, the very year that Jesus was baptized by John, which anointed Him for His ministry. Since "Messiah" means "Anointed One," this was the exact fulfillment of Daniel's prophecy that the Messiah would appear in A.D. 27.

Now mark this fact: seventy weeks were assigned for the Jewish probationary time, but Christ appeared as the Messiah after sixty-nine weeks. That left the seventieth week for Christ to minister before the Jews' probation ended. What was to happen in the seventieth week? Daniel 9:27 tells us, "And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease."
The midst of the week would be three and a half prophetic days (literal years) from His baptism.

According to the Bible, the ministry of Jesus lasted for three and a half years. In the spring of A.D. 31, He was crucified and the veil of the temple was rent (Matthew 27:51), signifying the end of the sacrificial system. By His death, He caused them to cease. Another three and a half years would lead up to the end of the seventy weeks and the end of Jewish probation. During those three and a half years the disciples labored largely for the Jews. But in A.D. 34 the seventy weeks were ended; Stephen was stoned and the gospel began to go to the Gentiles. (See Acts 8:4) The Jews had rejected the gospel message and were no longer God's chosen people - just as Daniel had predicted. As a nation, they had been rejected by God as His chosen people.

Those who teach the rapture get their seven years' tribulation by lifting that seventieth week of Daniel's prophecy completely out of its context and shoving it far into the future. They claim it will be fulfilled after Christ comes to snatch away the righteous secretly. Incredible? Absolutely! But they must grasp desperately for some text to support their seven years. They agree that the sixty-nine weeks of Daniel 9:25 refer to the period before Christ's first advent, but then they insert a 2,000-year gap before the seventieth week is fulfilled. They allot 69 weeks plus 2,000 years plus one week, or a total of 2,490 years. By this devious manipulation of God's Word, they have extended the Jewish probation; and based upon this, they teach that all the sinful Jews will be saved in a great second chance after the "secret rapture" takes place. The tragedy of the rapture theory is that it takes these beautiful verses of Daniel 9:24-27 that predict with accuracy the birth of Jesus, His baptism, and crucifixion, and applies them to Antichrist instead of Christ. They do this by stating that it is Antichrist that causes the sacrifice and oblation to cease after three and one-half years. But Daniel states that it is Jesus who caused the sacrificial system of the Jews to cease when He died on the cross. A misinterpretation that confuses something Christ has done and applies it to the devil instead, is certainly a tragic occurrence. And yet this is the only way they can arrive at a seven-year tribulation period. How sad!
